title: Low-Cal Middle Eastern Lentil Stew
subtitle: with Crusty Spice-Dusted Rolls
description: Think eating light means eating boring? Not in our book! Our low-cal recipes have all the punchy flavour and excitement you’d expect from us, and just 450 to 599 calories per serve.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Coarsely chop the onion. Halve the carrot lengthwise and cut into 2cm chunks. Cut the tomato into 2cm chunks. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves. Drain and rinse the lentils (see Cooking tip).

Soften onion: Heat 1½ tbs olive oil in a medium deep frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the onion and garlic, stirring, for 2-3 mins until softened. Add the kofta seasoning and ½ tsp dukkah and cook, stirring, for 30 secs or until fragrant. Add the lentils and cook, stirring, for 1 min or until warmed through.

Simmer stew: Add the carrot, tomato, 2 tbs tomato paste and 375ml (1½ cups) water to the pan and stir to combine. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to medium and cook, covered, for 15-20 mins until the carrot is tender and the sauce is slightly thickened. Taste, then season with salt and pepper. Remove the pan from the heat.

Grill rolls: Meanwhile, preheat the grill to high. Line an oven tray with foil. Tear the rolls in half widthwise, put on the lined tray and spray or lightly brush with olive oil. Scatter over 1 tsp dukkah (see Make it yours) and toss to coat. Grill the rolls, turning halfway, for 5-6 mins until golden and crisp.
Serve up: Divide the stew among bowls, scatter over ½ tsp dukkah and serve with the crusty rolls. Enjoy!

Make it yours: Dukkah is a Middle Eastern spice blend made up of almond, sesame seeds and spices like coriander and cumin. We've sprinkled it over the rolls before grilling them, but feel free to leave the rolls plain and serve the dukkah on the side.
